sources.title: The (Cyber) Center Cannot Hold: Futures, Bodies and Minds in William Gibson’s The Peripheral
sources.author: Carmen M. Mendez-Garcia, SFRA Review 50(4), 2020
sources.access_method: Public setting paragraphs on the two futures read
sources.read_scope: Assembler reconstruction, unequal access to advanced bodies and the distinction between the rural stub and later London.
sources.limitations: Reconstruction and medical technology do not alone establish continuing household provision. The Jackpot death toll is not a nonworking rate.

sources.title: Review: Peripheral by William Gibson
sources.author: Jamie Marriage, hosted by Marianne de Pierres, 2015
sources.read_scope: The later future is called post-scarcity, separate from Flynne’s precarious world.
sources.limitations: Broad qualitative label; no allocation constitution. Host is not the review author, and surrounding website material is excluded.

sources.title: Gibson, William
sources.author: The Encyclopedia of Science Fiction contributors
sources.access_method: Identified Neuromancer, Count Zero and Bridge-sequence paragraphs read
sources.read_scope: Corporate power, cyberspace intelligences, the Bridge settlement and the informational Idoru.
sources.limitations: Interpretive overview, not economic proof. Its separate Peripheral paragraph inaccurately calls Flynne’s supposed activity drug beta-testing; that detail is not adopted. Secret AI power is presented as conjectural, not universal fact.

sources.title: All Tomorrow’s Parties
sources.author: Kara Babcock, Kara.Reviews, 2015
sources.access_method: Public review’s nanofax and setting discussion read
sources.read_scope: Lucky Dragon fabrication appears as a hint of a developing technological future.
sources.limitations: A service and an impending transformation do not establish an already settled post-nanofax society.

sources.title: William Gibson: Agency
sources.author: couchmagpie, 2022
sources.access_method: Public indexed Eunice and security-service discussion read
sources.read_scope: Eunice and the later klept future occupy different narrative contexts.
sources.limitations: No household allocation rules or autonomous AI welfare government established; other timelines must remain separate.

sources.title: Schismatrix
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.access_method: Public economic-conflict and later-surplus paragraphs read
sources.read_scope: Changing Shaper/Mechanist rivalry, later economic surplus and different transformations.
sources.limitations: Later abundance is not a uniform entitlement across every earlier faction or a human participation census.

decisions.reason: Later London has assembler reconstruction and a post-scarcity label, but the short sources do not establish continuing labor-independent household access.
decisions.analysis: Unequal commodities and klept power are relevant but do not fill the missing production-to-access mechanism. Earlier rural jobs and the Jackpot’s dead are not assigned to the later population.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper novel reading; reopen only on a concise material-economy account.

decisions.reason: Agency does not yet establish a distinct AI-controlled post-Jackpot allocation system.
decisions.analysis: Eunice in a stub is not automatically the ruler of 2136. Overlap with the earlier London future must be checked before adding a distinct point; neither lead is retained.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading and avoid inflation from another book in the same future.

decisions.reason: An orbital enclave and owned AI systems do not establish a continuing automation-funded provision arrangement for its population.
decisions.analysis: Wealth, cryogenic seclusion and powerful computers cannot substitute for a verified material access rule. No whole orbital economy is inferred from a family’s power.

decisions.reason: Corporate power and cyberspace activity do not themselves establish post-work distribution.
decisions.analysis: The quick account concerns hired operations and unequal power, without a demonstrated general support system or preserved unnecessary employment.

decisions.reason: Fragmented matrix intelligences do not supply an identified supported human leisure population.
decisions.analysis: AI self-awareness and virtual personhood are distinct from production and access. Their existence does not establish a denominator for human nonworking.

decisions.reason: A self-organized Bridge community is not by itself an automated provision society.
decisions.analysis: Informal settlement and resistance to corporate power do not establish technological replacement of subsistence labor.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a community comparison without reconstructing the novel.

decisions.reason: The short Idoru reference establishes a virtual celebrity, not broad nanotechnological household provision.
decisions.analysis: An informational person and advanced Tokyo do not establish the discovery lead’s economic mechanism.

decisions.reason: Nanofax is a developing service; the proposed completed successor economy is unverified.
decisions.analysis: Fabrication potential at the ending does not identify a settled population and realized access rules.

decisions.reason: Mechanist technology and factional rivalry do not establish one stable material-support system.
decisions.analysis: Later system-wide surplus cannot be imported into all earlier Mechanist settlements or treated as a guarantee.

decisions.reason: Shaper adaptation and later surplus do not establish a uniform post-work arrangement.
decisions.analysis: Biological modification does not automatically replace human work; the changing Shaper factions require actual distribution evidence.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper reading rather than generalizing the entire chronology.
